title: Replacing a name-based class lookup with an allow-list
summary: See rule DPK-SAST-749 fire on a synthetic Java loader, replace the name lookup with a fixed map, and verify the finding is gone on rescan.
concept: Class.forName resolves a class from a string at runtime. When that string comes from a request, a config value, or any input the program does not control, the caller chooses which code is loaded and constructed. The safe pattern is a fixed allow-list: input selects only from names the program already chose. This lesson pairs with pack rule DPK-SAST-749, which flags the lexical shape Class.forName( on one line. The rule is line-based and cannot prove data flow, so every hit is review-required: a constant name is a false positive.
objectives: Explain why a runtime class lookup from input selects code.
Recognise Class.forName in review and in scan findings, and tell a constant name from an input-driven one.
Replace the lookup with a fixed allow-list and verify by rescan.

practice.instruction: Import the starter file into one of your OWN projects, run a SAST scan, and find rule DPK-SAST-749. Read the finding, confirm where the class name comes from, apply the fix (a fixed allow-list map), upload the fixed file, and run SAST again to verify the finding is no longer observed.
practice.fixInstruction: Replace the name lookup with a fixed map of allowed names to classes, and reject any other name.

quiz.prompt: Why does a class lookup from input need an allow-list?
options: The lookup then selects which code is loaded, so input must not choose freely
Class names load more slowly than map keys
Java does not allow Class.forName with a string
quiz.explanation: The name decides the code that runs. A fixed map limits input to names the program already chose.

quiz.prompt: What does DPK-SAST-749 prove when it fires?
options: That the name comes from untrusted input
That a Class.forName call is on that line; the reviewer must confirm where the name comes from
quiz.explanation: The rule is lexical. It flags the call shape only, so the reviewer confirms the data source.
